Some 3DGS compression methods integrate the estimation to exploit temporal redundancy; here, we focus on robust compression regardless of the estimator. We concatenate groups of frames into one Gaussian set, augment each Gaussian with a frame index, and pass it to a static (i.e., non-temporal) 3DGS codec, converting temporal redundancy into spatial redundancy. Concatenated sets are spatially partitioned to limit memory. Our technique requires neither a motion model nor knowledge of the training method. Averaged over six N3DV sequences, all six static codecs achieve gains on tracked sets (-42.0% to -71.8% BD-rate) over per-frame coding. On untracked sets, all codecs except HGSC, which appears incompatible with our technique, remain competitive with per-frame coding (-3.5% to +5.0%). We further replace D-FCGS's I-frame coding with our technique while retaining its P-frame coding, yielding an overall BD-rate of -46.2%. We propose to visualize "trackedness" using an inter-frame similarity metric. The project is available at https://wcjj1236.github.io/d3dgs-benchmark.

papers.title: GAPS: Generative Active Pseudo-view Selection for Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.authors: Hongfei Zhu; Haochen Deng; Sitao Zhang; Ling Zhou
papers.abstract: Novel view synthesis from sparse observations is severely under-constrained. Although 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables real-time rendering, it produces floaters, broken geometry, and washed-out backgrounds when trained with few views. We propose an alternating optimization framework that uses a pre-trained image diffusion model to generate geometrically consistent pseudo-views for additional 3DGS supervision. Generation is constrained by depth-conditioned ControlNet, IP-Adapter style transfer, LoRA scene adaptation, and img2img structural anchoring. We introduce Generative Active Pseudo-view Selection (GAPS) to balance reconstruction informativeness and generative reliability when choosing target views. Its annealing schedule shifts from conservative interpolation early in training to exploratory extrapolation later, gradually covering unobserved regions. A dual-criterion admission gate and uncertainty-weighted losses reject unreliable generations, while density-adaptive DropGaussian reduces overfitting in complex scenes. On LLFF with 3/6/9 views, our method improves average PSNR over vanilla 3DGS by 0.40/0.89/0.70 dB. On Mip-NeRF 360 with 12/24 views, the gains are 1.18/0.80 dB. SSIM improves and LPIPS decreases in every setting. Ablations show that active selection and density-adaptive regularization are both necessary; only the full method reduces LPIPS below the no-pseudo-view baseline on unbounded 360-degree scenes.

papers.title: LINGO: Latent Initialization and Gradient Optimization for Sparse-view X-ray Novel View Synthesis and CT Reconstruction with 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.authors: Lifeng Xing; Dequan Jin; Kunpeng Bu; Peigeng He; Shihui Ying
papers.abstract: In novel view synthesis and Computed Tomography (CT) reconstruction with sparse-view X-ray imaging, insufficient angular coverage leads to structural ambiguity and accumulated noise. Integrating 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) with X-ray absorption physics can achieve promising results, but it suffers from noisy initialization, positional insensitivity, and weak gradients in low-density regions. In this paper, we propose a unified Latent Initialization and Gradient Optimization (LINGO) framework to address these issues. LINGO combines latent mask-space initialization with dynamic gradient optimization to improve point cloud structural completeness while accelerating training. It constructs voxel-level 3D filters from X-ray masks to robustly suppress background noise and provide reliable geometric priors. By employing an adaptive voxel scaling strategy and dynamically scaling loss, LINGO can adjust spatial resolution and explicitly amplify gradients in low-density structures. To evaluate the quality of initialization, we introduce the Initialization Point Cloud Structural Deviation (IPSD) metric. Experiments on the X3D dataset indicate that for the novel view synthesis task, LINGO improves the Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) by an average of 0.72 and 0.0039, respectively, over baselines under identical sparse-view settings, achieving comparable reconstruction quality within 5k steps to state-of-the-art models typically trained with 30k iterations. For the CT reconstruction task, LINGO also demonstrates consistent improvements, with average PSNR and SSIM gains of 0.36 and 0.0134. These results highlight LINGO's effectiveness in both accelerating training and enhancing reconstruction quality across different sparse-view imaging scenarios.

papers.title: Cube-Splat: High-Fidelity 360° Gaussian Splatting SLAM via Cubemap Factorization and Adjoint-Consistent Optimization
papers.authors: Xiangfei Guo; Hao Shi; Yufan Zhang; Zhonghua Yi; Yongqi Mao et al.
papers.abstract: Recent progress in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has enabled dense visual SLAM with pinhole cameras, yet most pipelines are not designed for panoramic imagery. We present Cube-Splat, the first panoramic GS-SLAM framework that factorizes each 360° frame into a cubemap of four fixed-orientation virtual pinhole views sharing a single optical center. By designating the front face as the primary pose state, we accumulate gradients from all faces via an adjoint mapping, thereby enabling multi-face observations to coherently update a single state while strictly preserving cross-view geometric consistency. Concurrently, our mapping module densifies and optimizes anisotropic Gaussians using aggregated cubemap rays for high-fidelity, dense reconstruction. Furthermore, to rigorously evaluate panoramic SLAM under diverse and challenging conditions, we introduce SynPano, a highly scalable, photorealistic synthetic dataset featuring parameterized complex trajectories and multi-modal ground truth. Extensive evaluations on two public benchmarks (PALVIO and OmniBlender) and our SynPano dataset, collectively encompassing both indoor and outdoor scenes, demonstrate that Cube-Splat achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance in tracking accuracy and reconstruction fidelity. Both the source code and the SynPano dataset are available at https://github.com/guoxf304/CubeSplat.

papers.title: Demonstration Synthesis from a Single Scan via Gaussian Splatting for Visuomotor Policy Learning
papers.authors: Beichen Wang; Yuen-Hei Yeung; V. R. Sridhar Devarakonda; Xuesu Xiao
papers.abstract: Training a visuomotor policy calls for abundant demonstrations that closely match the target environment, yet collecting them anew remains expensive. Existing demonstration synthesis methods reduce this cost but remain constrained by high manual effort, limited visual fidelity, or heavy reliance on physics simulators. This paper introduces GaussianFactory, a high-fidelity data engine that mass-produces demonstrations with a single video scan as its only human input and no physics engine in the generation loop. Specifically, GaussianFactory reconstructs the scene as an editable 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) replica and samples from the object-combination tasks the scene affords. For each task, it plans grasps and trajectories purely kinematically on the geometric reconstruction, rendering photorealistic demonstrations that visually match the target environment. Physical dynamics enter the pipeline only where contact force interactions dictate the outcome---during grasp formation, via a learned contact model pretrained once on an interaction dataset. To evaluate the downstream utility of the synthesized demonstrations, we implement an end-to-end scan-to-deployment workflow in two setups: a simulated scene that stands in for the real world to enable reproducibility, and a real-world workspace with a physical UR10e robot. In each setup, a standard diffusion policy trained solely on the synthesized demonstrations achieves 95.1% and 84.2% success rates, respectively.

papers.title: PhGS: Post-Hoc Pruning and Refinement of Single-View Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Reconstructions
papers.authors: Rinto Yagawa; Han Cheng; Dieter Schmalstieg; Hideo Saito; Shohei Mori
papers.abstract: Recent single-view feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) generation predicts a fixed number of Gaussians per camera ray, introducing severe spatial redundancy. Most existing compaction strategies target multi-view setups to exploit cross-view consistency and are incompatible with single-image models. Instead of retraining the base feed-forward network to directly output compact representations, our insight is to keep the base models frozen and apply post-hoc pruning and recurrent refinement to the generated Gaussians. Consequently, we propose a backbone-agnostic compaction pipeline for single-view feed-forward 3DGS that couples an importance-score-based pruning mechanism with a trainable, lightweight recurrent refinement module, which iteratively updates the surviving primitives to restore image quality. Our results demonstrate seamless integration with existing baselines while preserving novel-view rendering fidelity and achieving high memory reduction. Furthermore, our method supports flexible inference-time keep ratios for application needs.

papers.title: SemSafe-3DGS: Semantic Risk-Aware Active Navigation in Uncertain 3D Gaussian Splatting Maps
papers.authors: Amirhossein Mollaei Khass; Athanasios Cosse; Nader Motee
papers.abstract: Autonomous robots operating in partially observed environments must navigate safely while acquiring observations that improve future planning. Existing safety formulations generally reason primarily about geometry. Consequently, geometrically similar scene elements may induce comparable control responses despite having different semantic consequences. We present a semantic risk aware safe-active perception framework for navigation in attributed 3D Gaussian maps. Semantic attributes modulate an Average Value-at-Risk collision clearance model through class dependent risk weights, allowing safety-critical Gaussian primitives to receive greater influence in the composite barrier. The resulting weighted clearances are aggregated into a control barrier function, while a trajectory-relevant active perception barrier promotes observations that reduce geometric map uncertainty along the robot's anticipated motion. Both objectives are integrated in a unified CBF-QP that enforces semantic risk-aware collision avoidance as a hard constraint while relaxing information acquisition when it conflicts with safety or task progress. Experiments demonstrate efficient safety constraint, improved navigation through active perception, semantic dependent trajectory adaptation, and real-robot execution under Ackermann dynamics.

papers.title: View-Structured Conformal Prediction for 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.authors: Junzheng Chu; Bin Pan; Zhenwei Shi
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) renders novel views in real time, but an uncertainty heatmap does not certify that a rendered view meets a certain prediction coverage. We treat novel-view synthesis as structured regression and ask that, with probability at least $1-α$, RGB prediction boxes cover at least a $1-β$ fraction of pixels in a new view. We propose View-Structured Conformal Prediction (VSCP). It splits the pre-calibration scale into a spatial shape from the renderer and a transferable view-difficulty factor, which predicts the smallest view-wise multiplier that shape needs. A held-out quantile over views (View-CP) then gives finite-sample validity even when transferring to new scenes. The same factorization makes the analysis exact: a conformity score is the ratio of oracle to predicted view difficulty, and excess width separates into a test-side and a calibration-side term. Across 13 real scenes, pixel-pooled calibration reaches 89.9\% marginal pixel coverage but only 61.4\% view-event coverage at a 90\% target, while View-CP reaches 91.7--92.0\%. At matched coverage VSCP cuts width by 22.1\% against a constant scale, and matches a ten-model ensemble's 21.0\% reduction using only one model per scene and four rather than ten rasterization passes per query. VSCP also improves on the closest single-model baseline, the 3DGS-U field, by 4.7 points ($p=0.0225$). The view predictor transfers from bounded source families to all nine unbounded Mip-NeRF~360 scenes. There the full scale beats the constant scale with 20.7\% width saving on all nine scenes. It also keeps an 18.3\% saving under a different densification backbone and runs at 216--280 FPS on an RTX~4090.

papers.title: PRG-Fusion: Orchestrating Generative Priors with Reconstruction Evidence for Driving View Synthesis
papers.authors: Sipeng He; Jialei Chen; Zhen Fang; Dongchun Ren; Feng Zhao
papers.abstract: Synthesizing photorealistic driving videos along specified trajectories is essential for scalable closed-loop simulation. However, reconstructed scenes exhibit spatially varying degradation under viewpoint shifts, while generative refinement can alter reliable content and introduce geometric inconsistencies. We propose \mbox{\textbf{PRG-Fusion}}, a framework for driving view synthesis that uses reconstruction evidence to orchestrate generative priors across regions. Our key insight is that reconstruction reliability and available support should jointly determine how previously unseen regions are generated and reliable content is preserved. We derive pixel-wise Preserve, Repair, and Generate (PRG) labels from reconstruction evidence to distinguish reliable appearance, degraded but supported content, and regions with insufficient support. At inference, these labels serve as a unified routing policy for region-aware spatiotemporal synthesis, orchestrating 3DGS appearance preservation, LiDAR-guided structural correction, and video-prior-driven content completion across Preserve, Repair, and Generate regions, respectively. We then follow a two-stage training paradigm, first establishing geometric control from sparse LiDAR projections and subsequently learning appearance control from dense 3DGS renderings. Extensive experiments on Waymo demonstrate that \mbox{\textbf{PRG-Fusion}} achieves state-of-the-art overall performance in novel trajectory video synthesis, with superior visual quality and geometric fidelity while maintaining competitive view consistency under large trajectory shifts. Our project page is available at https://pre-cici.github.io/PRG-Fusion/

papers.title: FujinSplat: Seeing Through Smoke with RAW-Domain Gaussian Splatting
papers.authors: Gengjia Chang; Ziteng Cui; Shuhong Liu
papers.abstract: The appearance of a smoky scene is shaped by two processes that a camera records together: the participating medium alters scene radiance in a view-dependent way, and the image signal processor (ISP) then remaps the result through a nonlinear tone and color transformation. Recovering a clean 3D scene requires separating both. Per-view sRGB dehazing acts only after the ISP has entangled them; standard 3D reconstruction ignores the medium and absorbs it into scene geometry and radiance. FujinSplat addresses the problem in the RAW domain, where the two processes remain separable. A per-scene Base ISP is fitted from the scene's hazy RAW captures to its own camera renderings and then frozen, providing a fixed photometric anchor that performs no dehazing. Analyzing expert corrections reveals a compact, low-dimensional correction space identifiable from RAW alone. FujinSplat therefore fits per-view action answers at the training poses and trains a single scene-agnostic controller to regress them from RAW; the corrected views supervise one static 3D Gaussian representation, jointly with a bounded per-view residual that reconciles cross-view photometric inconsistencies. On the RealX3D real-world smoke benchmark FujinSplat clearly outperforms the strongest comparable baseline, ahead of both physics-based reconstruction and restoration-then-3DGS pipelines. Code is available at https://github.com/I2WM/FujinSplat.

papers.title: WorldSculpt: Generating Compositional Worlds from Grounded Videos
papers.authors: Muyao Niu; Jixuan He; Ruihan Yu; Lian Fu; Yonghao Yu et al.
papers.abstract: We study the problem of generating a compositional 3D representation of a cluttered scene containing hundreds of objects. The goal is to represent the scene as a collection of individual object meshes placed in a shared world frame, as required by downstream applications such as gaming, AR/VR, simulation, and robotics. This task is challenging in densely cluttered scenes, where objects heavily occlude one another and each view reveals only a fraction of their geometry. Geometry-based approaches typically reconstruct the scene as a single representation and leave incomplete geometry in occluded regions, while existing compositional methods with generative priors are largely limited to relatively simple scenes. We show that complex scenes with hundreds of objects can instead be generated compositionally by adapting a strong single-object 3D generative prior to multi-view observations. We instantiate this paradigm with Pixal3D, extending it with a multi-view conditioning pathway that grounds object generation in multiple posed observations. Although the model is finetuned entirely on single objects in canonical space, it generalizes to large scenes with severe occlusion without any scene-level training, demonstrating the feasibility and scalability of this paradigm. We further introduce UE-MeshyScene, a photorealistic benchmark of densely cluttered scenes with hundreds of objects, per-object annotations, and ground-truth meshes. Across single-object, controlled multi-object, and UE-MeshyScene evaluations, our method consistently outperforms prior approaches, with larger gains as scene complexity and occlusion increase. Finally, we demonstrate broader applicability by converting generated 3DGS worlds, such as Marble and HY-World 2.0, into compositional mesh scenes.

papers.title: TileGS: Tile-Local Depth Binning for Gaussian Splatting Rasterization
papers.authors: Wei Tan; Matias Turkulainen; Lauri Ilola; Hamed Rezazadegan Tavakoli; Juho Kannala
papers.abstract: Real-time 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) achieves high rendering quality, but standard rasterization still traverses a globally sorted tile stream that creates long per-tile ranges and heavy geometry-attribute traffic. We present TileGS, a tile-local reorganization of Gaussian splatting. TileGS turns each long tile range into a sequence of shorter depth-local ranges, rasterizes those ranges in front-to-back order, and applies selective repair where coarse ordering is insufficient to match baseline compositing. Across a 9-scene benchmark on desktop and laptop Ada GPUs, our default No-GW (No Geometry-Write) variant delivers a mean 1.44x raster-kernel speedup on RTX 4090 and mean end-to-end frame speedups of 1.069x on RTX 4090 and 1.094x on RTX 1000 Ada over gsplat--a widely used optimized open-source 3DGS implementation--while matching the gsplat output up to numerical noise (|Delta PSNR| < 0.001 dB, |Delta SSIM| < 0.001, |Delta LPIPS| < 0.001). Full-suite RTX 4090 Nsight Compute profiling reveals TileGS is faster despite lower SM throughput, lower active-warp occupancy, and higher DRAM traffic, while total SASS thread instructions fall by 1.26x. Source-attributed profiling confirms that geometry attributes dominate the remaining memory pressure (85.8% of total raster traffic and 88.6% of excess sectors). Together, these counters support the interpretation that TileGS improves raster performance by reducing effective raster traversal work, rather than by reducing byte volume, improving coalescing, increasing occupancy, or directly reducing measured warp divergence.

papers.title: LightBridge: Feed-Forward Generative Relighting for 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.authors: Hezhi Cao; Panhao Cheng; huangsheng du; Qibiao Li; Youcheng Cai et al.
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) achieves high-quality, real-time novel view synthesis, but the resulting assets have baked-in illumination and cannot be easily relit. Inverse rendering methods optimize simplified reflectance and illumination models for each scene, limiting efficiency and relighting quality. Recent generative approaches leverage large diffusion models for realistic lighting edits, but applying them to 3DGS typically requires an additional per-scene optimization stage to bake the edited appearance into the representation. We present LightBridge, a feed-forward generative framework for controllable relighting of complete 3DGS assets in a single pass. To enable feed-forward training, we construct a large-scale Multi-Illumination Relighting Dataset with paired source and target observations of the same scenes. Latent Bridge Relighting Diffusion models relighting as source-to-target transport in latent space, enabling one-step extraction of 2D visual tokens without iterative diffusion sampling. A Gaussian Propagation Transformer uses a point transformer with sparse image-to-point self-attention followed by point-to-image cross-attention to efficiently propagate these cues across the complete 3DGS, while avoiding full attention over all image and Gaussian tokens. Experiments validate these designs, demonstrating competitive relighting quality and efficient single-pass prediction of complete relit 3DGS assets without scene-specific optimization. The code and dataset will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

papers.title: CapFrame: Text-Instructed Viewpoint Grounding in 3D Gaussian Scenes via Geometric Pseudo Labels
papers.authors: Jirong Li; Satoshi Ikehata; Shuhei Kurita; Ikuro Sato
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables photorealistic real-time novel view synthesis, yet placing a virtual camera to capture a desired frame remains largely manual. Existing language-guided approaches in 3D scenes mainly focus on object-centric grounding, determining what to observe but rarely controlling how it should appear in a single frame, such as subject orientation or frame layout. To address this limitation, we introduce a new task, Text-Instructed Viewpoint Grounding (TIVG), which aims to identify a 6-DoF camera pose in a 3D Gaussian scene whose rendered frame aligns with a text instruction. To solve this task, we propose CapFrame, a partially differentiable framework that converts language into geometric pseudo labels for camera pose optimization. CapFrame follows a Retrieve-Translate-Refine pipeline: it retrieves relevant views and ranks them through a Question-Evaluation process with MLLMs, translates the instruction into orientation and layout pseudo labels, and refines the camera pose via differentiable optimization with layout and orientation losses in 3DGS. Experiments on 38 real-world scenes with 135 instructions indicate that CapFrame produces viewpoints better aligned with texts than heuristic viewpoint search and adapted trajectory generation baselines, validated by VLM metrics, MLLM judges, and user studies. Code is available at: https://github.com/jirongli/CapFrame

papers.title: GhostSplat: Input-Triggered Backdoors for Multi-View-Consistent 3D Content Manipulation in Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting
papers.authors: Yudong Gao; Zongjian Ding; Linghan Chen; Yajing Chen; Yu Xinglin et al.
papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) reconstructs a 3D scene from sparse images in one forward pass. Its shared pretrained weights also expose a supply-chain attack surface. Existing Neural Radiance Field and 3DGS backdoors modify individual scenes and activate at selected viewpoints; they do not install persistent behavior in shared generator weights. We introduce GhostSplat, an input-triggered backdoor that installs such behavior in feed-forward 3DGS. A low-amplitude pattern added to the input images causes the poisoned generator to render an attacker-chosen payload on unseen victim scenes. Anchoring the payload to a 3D point and reprojecting it into each target view makes the payload multi-view consistent. Exact projection onto the generator's representation-specific consistency set leaves a realized payload unchanged because the output already belongs to that set. The GhostSplat training framework succeeds across three architectures (MVSplat, pixelSplat, DepthSplat) and two datasets (RealEstate10K, ACID). Its strongest evaluated injection and deletion settings reach 96% and 100% ASR, respectively, with zero observed false positives while surviving JPEG, blur, and resampling. Defenses that use only that exact projection are therefore insufficient; effective mitigation requires information or intervention beyond same-set consistency projection.

papers.title: ReconSplat: Generalizable 3D Scene Reconstruction Beyond Observed Views
papers.authors: Giuseppe Stracquadanio; Kevin Raj; Julia Grabinski; Stefan Roth
papers.abstract: We introduce ReconSplat, a feed-forward model for 3D scene reconstruction that aims to address the longstanding trade-off between plausible view generation for unobserved regions and geometric consistency, providing both geometrically aligned novel views and sharp depth estimates. Our approach builds on 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) as an intermediate differentiable scene representation and integrates it with a multi-view latent diffusion model (MV-LDM) trained to act simultaneously as a refiner and an inpainter for appearance and scene geometry. We enforce geometric consistency by guiding the diffusion process with variational 3D latent features for appearance and geometry, encoded by the feed-forward 3DGS representation and rasterized to 2D latent space. ReconSplat produces both photorealistic novel views and accurate depth maps on real-world benchmarks, RealEstate10K and DL3DV-10K, outperforming existing methods in challenging extrapolation setups. Notably, ReconSplat allows the extrapolation of unseen and challenging viewpoints jointly with coherent and precise scene geometry.

papers.title: Fast and Compact 3D Gaussian Splatting with Polarized Opacity Prior
papers.authors: Zi-Ming Wang; Kai-Wen Duan; Kowei Huang; Akihiro Sugimoto; Shang-Hong Lai
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) achieves state-of-the-art rendering quality at real-time speeds but suffers from "model bloat" - a large number of redundant, low-opacity Gaussians that inflate memory usage and training costs. This inefficiency stems from the standard "densify-then-prune" paradigm, which expands the model aggressively before relying on pruning to achieve compactness. To mitigate this problem, we present an efficient training framework that builds an intrinsically compact representation, replacing the conventional densify-then-prune cycle. Our method leverages a synergistic design: an L2 reconstruction loss to provide error-proportional gradients that stabilize optimization, and a novel Polarized Opacity Prior (POP) to actively manage the Gaussian population. POP steers informative primitives toward full opacity and uninformative ones toward transparency, enabling natural pruning and accelerating rendering through Early Ray Termination. Experiments on three public datasets demonstrate that our approach consistently achieves accelerated 3DGS training with significantly fewer Gaussians while maintaining comparable visual reconstruction quality. These results show that the proposed framework provides a simple and effective path toward fast and inherently compact 3DGS training.

papers.title: GaussVid: Sparse-View Gaussian Splatting with 3D-Aware Video Diffusion Priors
papers.authors: Xinhui Liu; Can Wang; Wei Jiang; Wei Wang; Dong Xu
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has achieved remarkable success in novel view synthesis; however, reconstructions under sparse views often exhibit noticeable artifacts. While recent video diffusion models provide strong spatio-temporal priors for 3DGS restoration, directly fine-tuning them for restoration is suboptimal, as they lack awareness of the underlying multi-camera geometry, resulting in multi-view inconsistencies. In this work, we propose a novel 3D-aware video restoration framework designed to enhance the quality of sparse 3DGS reconstruction. Specifically, we construct a large-scale 3DGS video dataset to enable specialized fine-tuning. To bridge the gap between 2D video generation and 3D multi-view constraints, we introduce a camera-conditioned geometric prior. By using the first and last frames as boundary anchors and encoding the corresponding camera relationships, we explicitly inject spatial structure into the video generation pipeline. This boundary-anchored, camera-aware prior guides the network toward geometrically grounded restoration that remains coherent across viewpoints. Extensive experiments show that, among video-prior restoration methods, our approach attains the best pixel- and structure-level fidelity (PSNR/SSIM) and improves multi-view consistency, while remaining competitive in perceptual quality (LPIPS).

papers.title: Fusion-Aware Direct 3D Gaussian Generation with Structured Patch Latent Flows
papers.authors: Yizhao Wang; Jingbo Wang; Guantao Zhang
papers.abstract: Class-guided 3D object generation is important for intelligent content creation, virtual environments, and digital asset design. Although 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) offers an explicit and render-efficient representation, directly generating 3D Gaussian objects is difficult because Gaussian primitives are unordered, variable-sized, locally dense, and highly sensitive to rendering. Existing 3DGS generation methods usually depend on multi-view synthesis, reconstruction, or lifted 2D priors, fusing information mainly from observed views rather than modeling the intrinsic structural distribution of 3D Gaussian objects.   This paper proposes a fusion-aware hierarchical Gaussian patch representation for direct class-guided 3DGS generation with rectified flow. Irregular Gaussian sets are decomposed into canonical local patches and encoded as structured tokens. The resulting hierarchical latent space fuses global class semantics, patch-level geometry and appearance, spatial correspondence, and rendering-sensitive cues. On this basis, we design a structure-aware rectified flow model with patch-position conditioning, global-local coupled velocity prediction, and density-aware velocity weighting, enabling direct latent generation of class-conditioned 3DGS objects within seconds. A render-feedback fusion strategy further aligns latent flow learning with decoded multi-view rendering quality.   Experiments show that the proposed method generates 3D Gaussian objects with more coherent geometry, sharper local details, and better multi-view consistency than baseline latent generative models. Ablation studies confirm the contributions of hierarchical information fusion, global-local coupling, density-aware supervision, and render-feedback learning while preserving practical sampling efficiency overall.

papers.title: OccamView: Object-Conditioned View Selection for Frame-Budgeted Active 3D Gaussian Reconstruction
papers.authors: Hongbo Gao; Wei Zhang; Zeyu Ni; Dihao Zhu; Ruifeng Li et al.
papers.abstract: Active 3D Gaussian reconstruction fundamentally relies on selecting informative next-best views under limited sensing budgets. Existing active 3DGS methods primarily plan viewpoints according to geometric information gain, treating object-induced hidden regions in the same manner as general unexplored space. Under tight frame budgets, such geometry-driven strategies may prioritize global scene coverage while leaving partially observed objects incompletely reconstructed. To address this limitation, we propose OccamView, an object-conditioned view-selection framework for frame-budgeted active 3D Gaussian reconstruction. Rather than predicting unseen object geometry or performing shape completion, OccamView maintains an online object memory from open-vocabulary detections grounded in measured RGB-D observations and represents unresolved local occupancy around detected objects as conservative hidden-region proxies. Candidate viewpoints are then evaluated using an occlusion-aware proxy-coverage score. Furthermore, we introduce a Geo-Floor mechanism that restricts object-conditioned re-ranking to geometrically competitive candidates, allowing object-conditioned cues to guide complementary observations while preserving the geometry-driven exploration behavior of the underlying planner. Experiments on Replica and Matterport3D under a unified frame-budgeted protocol show that OccamView consistently reduces Completion and improves Completion Ratio across five frame budgets, with particularly pronounced gains under limited frame budgets. These results demonstrate that lightweight object-conditioned cues effectively complement geometry-driven active view planning.

papers.title: Gaussian-JEPA: Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning for 3D Gaussian Splats
papers.authors: Bin Ren; Qi Ma; Yue Li; Zongyan Han; Yidi Li et al.
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) represents 3D content with anisotropic primitives that jointly encode geometry and appearance. Fixed-budget encoders consume sampled observations of Gaussian assets, so the same object may be observed through different primitive realizations. Existing self-supervised methods mainly reconstruct masked Gaussian attributes, tying supervision to one sampled realization and requiring an input-space decoder. Latent prediction offers an alternative, but its application to Gaussian tokens requires targets that accommodate coupled attributes and heterogeneous spatial support. We introduce Gaussian-JEPA, which predicts representations of held-out Gaussian token blocks from visible context. An online encoder processes the context, while a shared exponential-moving-average encoder supplies stop-gradient features for multi-scale targets. Complementary target projections and feature-space grounding provide latent supervision without reconstructing Gaussian attributes. We evaluate the features under Gaussian resampling, partial observations, and renderable shape completion, together with transfer to part segmentation and object classification. Compared with matched reconstruction pretraining, Gaussian-JEPA is more consistent across resampled inputs, retains more instance information under partial observations, and provides stronger frozen features for Gaussian completion. These results support latent prediction as an effective objective for reusable 3D Gaussian representations. Code is on the project page (https://amazingren.github.io/Gaussian-JEPA/).

papers.title: LocusGS: Spatially Grounded Tokens for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.authors: Wenyu Li; Sidun Liu; Tongrui Hu; Peng Qiao; Yong Dou
papers.abstract: Recent query-based feed-forward 3DGS methods represent a scene using learnable queries, each aggregating multi-view evidence and decoding a group of Gaussians. Ideally, different queries should specialize in coherent local regions of the scene. However, we observe that Gaussians decoded from the same query often scatter across distant scene regions, resulting in weak query-level spatial coherence and poor alignment with the scene structure. We attribute this behavior to the purely latent representation of existing Gaussian queries. To address this limitation, we introduce LocusGS, which augments each Gaussian query with a 3D anchor state consisting of a center and a support radius. The anchor state is progressively refined across decoder layers and is used throughout query interaction, multi-view feature aggregation, and Gaussian generation. Specifically, an anchor-to-ray geometric bias guides each query toward spatially relevant image observations, while anchor-centered decoding organizes its Gaussians within a local region. Experiments on novel view synthesis benchmarks show that LocusGS improves rendering quality over query-based Gaussian token baselines under the same Gaussian budget. Further analysis shows that the learned anchors form coherent spatial layouts and lead to more structured Gaussian distributions, demonstrating that explicit anchor states improve the spatial organization. Our project page: https://leo-frank.github.io/LocusGS_viewer.

papers.title: CausalSplat: Towards Comprehensive Hierarchical Reasoning in 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.authors: Jiayu Ding; Meilu Song; Yun Chen; Wei Gao; Ge Li
papers.abstract: While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has advanced open vocabulary scene understanding, existing methods remain confined to explicit queries. They struggle to interpret implicit intents, complex spatial constraints, and commonsense reasoning required for practical embodied interactions. To address this gap, we introduce the task of reasoning 3D Gaussian segmentation and construct two benchmarks, Causal-LERF and Causal-ScanNet. These benchmarks systematically evaluate commonsense, spatial, affordance, and counterfactual reasoning. Evaluations reveal that current state of the art methods perform poorly on these reasoning challenges. Therefore, we propose CausalSplat, a framework that integrates vision-language models with 3D scene graphs to disentangle explicit structural perception from implicit logical inference. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CausalSplat achieves state of the art performance on our reasoning benchmarks while showing strong generalizability on standard referring and open vocabulary 3D segmentation tasks. Project Page: https://jiayuding031020.github.io/CausalSplat

papers.title: Learning Gaussian Structure: Intervention-Guided Density Control for Feed-Forward Driving Reconstruction
papers.authors: Hang Li; Jiahe Li; Meiying Gu; Jin Zheng; Lina Yu et al.
papers.abstract: Feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction has recently emerged as an efficient approach for driving scene reconstruction. However, prevailing LiDAR-based methods preserve the initial correspondence between observed points and Gaussian primitives, treating the initialized primitive set as the final representation. Unlike optimization-based 3DGS, these methods cannot accumulate gradients during training to determine how the scenes representation should be densified. Meanwhile, the shared sparse backbone only fuses observations from different timestamps implicitly, without explicitly aggregating cross-time evidence for individual primitives. In this paper, we present Learning Gaussian Structure (LGS), a framework that enhances both Gaussian structure and primitive attributes. Our key observation is that changes in local gradient responses induced by a prune or add intervention reveal whether the corresponding structural adjustment benefits reconstruction. Based on this observation, our Gaussian Densify Policy learns a Densify Map comprising Prune and Addition Scores from controlled interventions, and directly adjusts the Gaussian structure during inference. We further develop a compact Cross-Time Point Query that explicitly retrieves and aggregates neighboring features from Gaussian primitives at other timestamps for reliable attribute prediction. Extensive experiments on the Waymo Open Dataset and PandaSet demonstrate that LGS consistently outperforms existing methods.

papers.title: TRACE-GS: On-Policy Trajectory Distillation with Privileged Geometric Conditioning for Sparse-View 3DGS Restoration
papers.authors: Linlian Jiang; Yuchen Xi; Sadman Rakib Pinon; Ruigang Yang; Yang Wang et al.
papers.abstract: We present TRACE-GS, an on-policy trajectory distillation framework that leverages privileged geometric conditioning at training time, thereby adapting a diffusion prior to sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) restoration. Rather than pursuing increasingly sophisticated restoration architectures, we identify a more fundamental limitation shared by existing diffusion-based approaches: supervision at independently noised states does not cover those reached during inference. In sparse-view 3DGS, under-constrained geometry biases denoising from the outset, and the resulting deviations compound along the rollout. TRACE-GS instead performs on-policy trajectory distillation: a teacher conditioned on richer geometry from additional training views supplies targets along the sparse-view student's own rollout, aligning denoising directions and cross-view responses at each visited state. This training-only geometry places TRACE-GS in the learning using privileged information (LUPI) setting. At deployment, only the sparse-view student is retained, and its restored renderings serve as pseudo-observations for 3DGS refinement. To the best of our knowledge, TRACE-GS is the first to derive on-policy supervision from privileged geometry for sparse-view 3DGS restoration, achieving consistent gains and strong generalization across datasets and sparse-view settings.

papers.title: InstanceSplat: Instance-Aware Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting for Scene Understanding
papers.authors: Minchao Jiang; Xiaoxuan Ma; Shunyu Jia; Haoru Wang; Zhang Liang et al.
papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables efficient and generalizable 3D reconstruction, but current feed-forward 3DGS methods for scene understanding remain largely category-oriented. In contrast, instance-aware 3DGS methods typically rely on per-scene optimization and often decouple reconstruction from instance and semantic learning, limiting reciprocal interactions among them. We present InstanceSplat, a unified feed-forward 3DGS framework for generalizable 3D reconstruction and instance-aware scene understanding from pose-free multi-view images. In a single forward pass, InstanceSplat constructs an instance-aware Gaussian representation that jointly encodes appearance, geometry, instance identity, and language-aligned semantics. Shared 3D Gaussians ground instance identities across views, producing renderable and cross-view-consistent instance features. To allow reconstruction and scene understanding to benefit from each other, we further design an instance-centric learning strategy that connects reconstruction, instance learning, and semantic learning through shared instance structure. Specifically, instance cues guide reconstruction, language-aligned semantics strengthen the discrimination of confusing same-category instances, and instance regions aggregate semantic evidence into coherent object-level predictions. Experiments on novel-view synthesis, instance segmentation, and open-vocabulary semantic understanding under varying input-view settings and on an unseen dataset demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, practical efficiency, and strong generalization.

papers.title: The Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model as a Statistical Model: Identification, Estimation, and Model Comparison
papers.authors: Zihao Cao
papers.abstract: The random intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM) distinguishes stable differences between people from lagged associations within individuals. We use a matrix representation to study its statistical properties for p variables measured across T waves. We derive a necessary and sufficient rank condition for global identification when transition matrices and innovation covariances vary by wave. Under time-invariant transitions, the condition specifies when three waves suffice. For complete Gaussian trajectories, matrix differentiation yields the profile likelihood score for each covariance and transition block. We also derive the population parameters of the conventional cross-lagged panel model (CLPM) when an RI-CLPM with fixed parameters generates the data. Our formulas quantify how CLPM slopes for observed variables differ from RI-CLPM slopes for within-person deviations at each transition. When the RI-CLPM transition matrix is time-invariant, the comparison also covers CLPM slopes pooled across waves. The formulas recover earlier bivariate results and show when cross-lagged slopes can appear, cancel, reverse sign, or change their ordering across models.

papers.title: SurgGenesis: A Generative Surgical World Model for Future-Aware Surgical Understanding
papers.authors: Qirui Zhong; Quande Liu; Yang Chen; Cheng Xue
papers.abstract: Surgical scene understanding is constrained by data scarcity and long-tail class imbalance, as annotating surgical videos demands scarce clinical expertise while rare procedural events remain underrepresented. We tackle this through data generation and propose SurgGenesis, a generative surgical world model that learns future surgical state transitions in a latent space from visual observations and textual procedural descriptions, serving as a scalable surgical data engine. To adapt a large-scale video diffusion model to the data-scarce surgical domain without catastrophic forgetting, we introduce a three-stage progressive LoRA strategy that incrementally injects endoscopic visual priors, procedural semantics, and spatial motion cues. Rather than judging generation by visual fidelity alone, we validate SurgGenesis along two axes that separate a world model from a generic generator: (i) future-awareness, by comparing predicted futures against the real future through a GT-latent prediction gap and temporal-horizon analysis, and (ii) action-faithful usefulness, by checking that generated clips contain the commanded surgical triplet and that using them to rebalance long-tail events and drive downstream understanding (segmentation, triplet recognition, 3D reconstruction) yields action-specific gains. Conditioned futures therefore complement conventional long-tail sampling. Code: https://zh-qr.github.io/SurgGenesis

papers.title: Instant LiDAR: Feed-Forward Gaussian Reconstruction for LiDAR Simulation
papers.authors: Xin Kang; Jiahui Huang; Jiawei Ren; Sipeng Zhang; Yu Chen et al.
papers.abstract: LiDAR reconstruction supports closed-loop autonomous driving simulation, but hours of per-scene optimization make large asset libraries costly to build and maintain. We present Instant LiDAR, a feed-forward pipeline that reconstructs multiple LiDAR scans as reusable Gaussian assets in minutes without per-scene optimization. LiDAR measurements provide strong geometric priors, but directly initializing Gaussians from them yields poor reconstruction due to nonuniform sampling and a limited field of view. Sparse returns leave surface gaps, while combining scans expands coverage but introduces redundant primitives. To address these challenges, Instant LiDAR combines measurement-anchored Gaussian prediction, sampling-aware Gaussian scales, and multi-frame consolidation. The predictor refines attributes anchored to recorded returns, while the scales adapt spatial support to LiDAR sampling. Multi-frame consolidation merges overlapping predictions into a compact asset spanning the driving log. Compared with NuRec, Instant LiDAR reconstructs scenes approximately 46 times faster on Physical AI (PAI) and 70 times faster on Waymo. It also achieves comparable downstream 3D detection accuracy on Waymo.

papers.title: Classical phase space distributions for quantum states in cosmology: General states, operator ordering and the geometry of fading non-commutativity
papers.authors: Alejandro Corichi
papers.abstract: In earlier work with Ashtekar and Kesavan we showed that, for linear fields in any FLRW background, the vacuum defines a probability distribution $ρ_o$ on the classical phase space whose moments are exactly the Weyl-ordered $n$-point functions. We extend that analysis in four directions. First, for an arbitrary state $Ψ$ we give an explicit formula, in the Bargmann representation, for the distribution $ρ_Ψ$ that reproduces all Weyl-ordered expectation values. For pure states it is non-negative precisely for coherent and squeezed states, each the Gaussian of a compatible Kähler metric, and the Gaussian smoothing needed to make it positive is either zero or the full coherent-state width. Second, for linear observables every operator ordering differs from the Weyl ordering by explicit products of $c$-number commutators. Third, for two linear observables in a pure Gaussian state, the classical correlation coefficient, the ratio of commutator to anticommutator and the squeezing are functions of a single angle between their Hamiltonian vector fields; this bounds the departure of arbitrarily ordered $n$-point functions from the moments of $ρ$. Fourth, for fields in FLRW the equality holds at arbitrary, possibly different, times and for every homogeneous isotropic quasi-free state. In de Sitter the non-commutative corrections fall as $e^{-N}$ for field and momentum and as $e^{-3N}/3$ for the field at two times. For the state inherited from inflation they stay suppressed in the radiation era, by the inverse occupation number, except near the nodes of the mode functions. The same squeezing entangles the modes $\pm\vec k$ relative to the radiation-era vacuum and makes displaced-parity measurements violate Bell inequalities, so the positive distribution describes a specified family of observables, not all measurements.

papers.title: Tortho-Gaussian++: Suppressing Geometric Drift and Floaters for Robust Gravity-Aligned TDOM Generation in Large-Scale Aerial Scenes
papers.authors: Xiang Wang; Xin Wang; Zongqian Zhan
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has demonstrated remarkable performance in aerial scene reconstruction, motivating its recent extension to true digital orthophoto maps (TDOMs) generation. We propose Tortho-Gaussian++, a novel 3DGS training framework that suppresses geometric drift and floaters and automatically prunes unreliable peripheral regions, coupled with a robust gravity-aligned TDOM rendering solution. First, we explore geometric support via viewing-ray-based geometric observability analysis, quantitatively characterizing the reliability for each Gaussian and subsequently pruning peripheral regions with particularly weak geometric support. Second, the optimizer state initialization is refined for newly created Gaussians during densification, intrinsically suppressing drift and floaters without external priors. Lastly, a robust gravity direction estimation solution is designed, combining image-derived gravity cues, camera-distribution priors and nadir views, to achieve a gravity-aligned orthogonal projection reference for TDOM rendering. Extensive experiments on multiple large-scale UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) datasets demonstrate that our Tortho-Gaussian++ outperforms vanilla 3DGS by 0.5-3.5 dB in average PSNR and yields comparable or superior performance to prior-guided 3DGS methods. Notably, it reduces the training time, VRAM and Gaussian number by 45.5%, 47.2%, and 58.6%, respectively. Qualitative evaluations confirm that our method effectively suppresses drift and floaters, while robust gravity direction estimation reduces tilt-induced facade artifacts in TDOMs.

papers.title: SprintGS: Eliminating Redundancy for Fast 3D Gaussian Splatting Training
papers.authors: Ryosuke Watanabe; Tomoaki Konno
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) renders photorealistic novel views in real time, but its per-scene training (optimization) remains slow. Recent fast training methods such as FastGS shorten training to a few minutes by reducing the number of Gaussians. Profiling FastGS, we find two costs that remain even in its compact model. First, rasterization is still the largest cost, and redundant work remains in it. Second, the loss computation does not shrink with the number of Gaussians, so its share of the training time grows as the model becomes compact. We present SprintGS, a training framework built on FastGS that keeps the model compact and reduces both costs. For rasterization, scheduled tile culling limits each Gaussian to the tiles where it matters, using a coarse footprint that is annealed to the exact one before training ends; convergence-aware pruning removes converged, nearly transparent Gaussians; and a shuffle-efficient backward pass reduces the data exchanged between GPU threads. For the loss, a fused loss computes the loss and its image gradient in the forward pass without a loss map, removing most of its cost. SprintGS trains 2.15x faster than FastGS at comparable quality, and 1.81x faster in its high-quality setting. It also accelerates other fast training methods and dynamic, sparse-view, and surface reconstruction.

papers.title: Efficient Scene-Distribution-Aware Second-Order Optimization for 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.authors: Hyunseung Son; Young Sun Choi; Youngsik Yun; Kibeom Hong; Youngjung Uh
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) optimization updates the Gaussian parameters one training view at a time, tens of thousands of times. Unlike such single-view updates, multi-view batches reduce dependence on individual training views, and second-order optimization reduces the number of updates with larger, structured parameter changes. Because fewer updates leave fewer chances to correct a change that fits only the views used in one update, scene coverage becomes more important for each second-order update. Multi-view second-order updates, however, are expensive. Pixel sampling reduces this cost, but two issues remain. First, selecting views without considering overlap leaves some views redundant. To address this, we propose a view selection strategy that reduces this redundancy. Second, existing work processes the sampled pixels of each view in a separate pass and recomputes alpha compositing for these pixels from scratch. We introduce two implementation strategies that reduce both overheads by processing the sampled pixels of multiple views in joint passes and reusing the transmittance and accumulated color cached during rendering. On three datasets, our method reaches higher PSNR than the sampled second-order baseline in less than half its optimization time, with competitive SSIM and LPIPS.

papers.title: VersionGS: Compact and Motion-Robust Dynamic Gaussian Splatting via Versioned Gaussians
papers.authors: Shihang Wei; Yichi Zhang; Fengqing Zhu
papers.abstract: Recent dynamic Gaussian splatting methods encode temporal change, either as smooth functions of time or as constrained updates between frames. We observe that their reconstruction quality degrades significantly under fast motion. In challenging dance sequences, their PSNR drops by 1.1-4.0 dB on high-motion frames compared to low-motion frames. To overcome this limitation, we propose VersionGS, a method that directly encodes per-frame Gaussian states and uses motion estimation only to guide reconstruction. Within each group of frames, unchanged Gaussians keep their current versions in a shared dictionary, while modified Gaussians are appended as new versions. To maximize version reuse, we introduce selective sequential construction, which refines the Gaussians selected by optical flow, photograph differences or rendering errors and leaves the others unchanged. The dictionary is then pruned, fine-tuned with simulated quantization and encoded as images. Adjusting the pruning ratio trades off storage and quality without rebuilding the dictionary. On the fast dance sequences of DanceNet3D, VersionGS improves foreground PSNR by 2.7 dB over the best baseline, and its PSNR decreases by less than 0.3 dB on the highest-motion frames. On N3DV and Technicolor, it requires 6.0x and 5.7x less storage than TAD-GS, the strongest baseline overall, while achieving even higher PSNR. Finally, playback is fast and requires no motion model or neural network, only a 3DGS rasterizer.

papers.title: AnyPrune: Optimization-Free Pruning for Any Feedforward 3D Gaussian Splatting Pipeline
papers.authors: Nicola Leonetti; Federico Stella; Aoxiang Fan; Saqib Javed; Pascal Fua et al.
papers.abstract: Feedforward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) pipelines reconstruct a scene from images in a single forward pass, representing it as real-time-renderable 3D Gaussians. However, the resulting representations contain far more Gaussians than are needed to render the scene faithfully, especially when there are many input views. This drastically increases memory and storage requirements. Existing pruning methods either require costly re-optimization, which defeats the purpose of a single forward pass, or rely on simple strategies that do not exploit all the available information. We present AnyPrune, a transformer-based, optimization-free pruning module designed to work on top of any feedforward 3DGS pipeline. To remove unnecessary Gaussians, AnyPrune learns and exploits pipeline-specific redundancy patterns through a short single-GPU training on the frozen target feedforward pipeline. AnyPrune achieves better rendering quality than existing optimization-free pruning methods in most settings and generalizes to unseen datasets, as shown through extensive experiments across multiple feedforward pipelines, datasets, and input view counts. It prunes a 1.6M-Gaussian field in about $5\,\mathrm{s}$ on a consumer GPU, faster than every method that merges Gaussians or re-optimizes the field. It can also be combined with the pruning built into feedforward pipelines, pruning further at moderate ratios while preserving or improving rendering quality. Finally, it can even suggest a scene-specific pruning ratio that retains most of the quality.

papers.title: Completion-Aware Compression for Progressive 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.authors: Reagan Koo; Yeong-Gyu Kim; Eun-Seok Ryu
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables high-quality novel-view rendering, but its large scene representations are costly to transmit. Pruning and compression reduce file sizes, yet progressive delivery also requires usable reconstructions before the full scene arrives. Existing progressive representations provide partial scenes, but level-based updates are limited by predefined coding boundaries. This paper presents a progressive 3DGS codec that balances attribute fidelity with the image benefit of making Gaussians available earlier. Its single compact stream supports partial 3D reconstruction and adds newly decoded Gaussians as more bytes arrive. The stream supports fine-grained updates at arbitrary received-byte budgets, without separate encodings or later attribute refinement. At matched complete-file sizes and received bytes, completion-aware allocation improves 1/8 PSNR over attribute-only allocation by 0.48-1.43 dB. The proposed codec compresses original 3DGS representations by 62-88 times while retaining near-reference Full PSNR. Under the evaluated 50-Mbps delivery model, partial reconstruction becomes available in approximately 0.2 s.

papers.title: NRG-Twins: Pixel-Level Ground Truth for Rigidity Violations in Generated Videos
papers.authors: Chenrui Fan; Qiyang Hu; Luca Scharr; Paolo Favaro
papers.abstract: Video generators now produce realistic clips of scenes and objects, which makes generated video an attractive source of 3D content. Yet generated video is not 3D consistent: static content slowly deforms or slides, 3D reconstruction degrades, and the errors are too subtle to label by hand. To make generators 3D consistent, or to build rewards and guidance that push them there, we need data that say where and by how much a generated video breaks rigidity, and these data must come from generated video itself. We obtain per-pixel ground-truth labels from real-generated twins: a real clip paired with its re-creation by a keyframe-conditioned video generator. After inserting real keyframes so that the twin camera roughly follows the real one, we measure per pixel, in degrees, how far the twin departs from a rigid scene seen along its own camera path. We release Non-Rigidly Generated Twins (NRG-Twins), 871 twins, the code that builds them for new generators, and a benchmark with an official test split. A detector trained on these data, the Non-Rigidly Generated Pixel Detector (NRG-PD), predicts the per-pixel angle from RGB alone. It separates inconsistent from consistent pixels with AUROC 0.85, against 0.40-0.74 for seven existing consistency and motion-segmentation methods, and its predictions improve 3DGS of video that contains generated content.

papers.title: View Management with Gaussian Placement and Opacity Regularization for Online 3DGS
papers.authors: Dong Hwi Kim; Park Sangwon; Chaehyeon Song; Ayoung Kim
papers.abstract: The realistic rendering of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has drawn interest from real-time applications that require maps to be built online. This led to coupling 3DGS with SLAM, providing camera poses and initial Gaussians for the map. However, the map is still optimized with designs inherited from conventional SLAM, which train only on keyframes selected for localization and regularize geometry with uncertain frontend depth. These designs overlook the model complexity of a 3DGS map: with millions of parameters but few views of each region, the map overfits to sparse inputs. Resolving this is challenging, as every view and Gaussian added to the map competes for the same real-time budget. We close this gap from both sides. To add views while keyframes preserve the structure of the map, we progressively admit non-keyframe images as mapping updates complete and allocate the limited updates across different groups of frames according to the supervision each group provides. To control the model complexity of the map, edge-guided initialization places new Gaussians where image detail requires them. To complement the uncertain frontend depth, Self-Referenced Opacity Regularization (SOR) uses accumulated rendering evidence, at no extra rendering cost, to suppress the opacity of Gaussians that persistently contribute in front of a map-derived surface reference. Together, these designs improve both the appearance and the geometry of online maps within the real-time budget.

papers.title: HiGS: A Hierarchical Architecture for Fast Differentiable 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.authors: Dawid Pająk; Martin Bisson; Rodolfo Lima; François Trudel
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) makes one screen tile the cell of partitioning, the cell of rasterization, and the unit of parallel work. Partitioning favors large tiles and rasterization small ones, and with one unit per tile the densest tiles set the frame time. We present Hierarchically Tiled Gaussian Splatting (HiGS), a unified architecture for rendering and reconstruction that gives each role its own granularity: Gaussians are partitioned over coarse macro-tiles, rasterized over the fine render tiles within them, and processed in bounded depth-sorted batches. A dense region issues more batches instead of one longer unit, so frame time follows the work in a view rather than its densest tile. The same batches carry reconstruction: compositing supplies the transmittance and color needed to differentiate each one independently, leaving optimizer memory traffic as the dominant training cost. We fuse the optimizer into the backward pass, halve the parameters and moments it stores and updates directly, and defer appearance updates outside the view. HiGS renders scenes faster than every published method we evaluate, by the widest margin on views with uneven load, and reconstructs them faster and in less memory, at equal image quality and with exact front-to-back alpha compositing.

papers.title: InterGS+: Inter-Frame Gaussian Splatting Compression with Geometry-Aware Transformer Prediction and Adaptive Residual Coding
papers.authors: Muhammad Talha; Zhu Li; Joel Jung
papers.abstract: Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) provides real-time photorealistic rendering, but representing each frame as irregular Gaussian primitives with high-dimensional attributes creates substantial storage and transmission cost. Exploiting temporal redundancy is challenging because Gaussian primitives do not preserve fixed identities across frames. We propose InterGS+, a lightweight post-hoc inter-frame codec that jointly improves temporal prediction and residual representation. Current-frame geometry is coded with G-PCC and reconstructed before prediction, enabling consistent temporal neighborhoods at encoder and decoder. Attributes are predicted using lightweight KNN and bilateral predictors together with a geometry-aware transformer for spherical-harmonic (SH) appearance, with per-Gaussian mode selection. Residual coding is adapted to each attribute: SH innovations are coded in a shared PCA domain using vector quantization with refinement, opacity and scale in activated gamma-companded domains, and rotation as canonicalized quaternion innovations using vector quantization and refinement. On MPEG dynamic sequences, InterGS+ achieves average BD-rate reductions of 45.48% over G-PCC Amd. 1 and 7.78% over InterGS-Lite, with corresponding BD-PSNR gains of 9.98 dB and 1.10 dB. Average decoding complexity is 0.049 ms/Gaussian, demonstrating efficient streamable dynamic 3DGS compression.

papers.title: Tornado4D: Physics-Guided 4D Gaussian Reconstruction of a Laboratory Tornado from Sparse One-Sided Videos
papers.authors: Yucheng Zhu; Maria J. Molina; Christopher Metzler
papers.abstract: Characterizing how tornadoes evolve over space and time is critically important for understanding and preparing for these highly destructive weather events. Towards this end, we develop algorithms capable of forming time-resolved 3D reconstructions of laboratory smoke tornadoes from sparse one-sided videos. Even in a controlled environment, reconstruction is severely underconstrained: appearance is view dependent, motion is non-rigid, and the unobserved volume admits many geometries. We present Tornado4D, a physics-guided 4D Gaussian framework capable of reconstructing laboratory tornadoes from sparse, one-sided videos. Tornado4D uses knowledge of the enclosure geometry to introduce rotational airflow field priors that constrain how the 3D structure evolves over time. These rotational priors allow us to reconstruct otherwise unobserved structure. We evaluate reconstruction accuracy by computing novel-view synthesis accuracy on a held out camera view: Tornado4D outperforms frame-by-frame 3DGS and video-based 4DGS by a considerable margin.

papers.title: Not All Directions Are Flat: Decomposed-Gradient Flatness for Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.authors: Ungbae Yoon; Kwanyoung Kim
papers.abstract: Many applications of novel view synthesis, such as augmented reality and robotics, can afford only a few input views, since dense capture is costly. With such sparse views, however, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) overfits the training views and degrades at unseen viewpoints. Among the approaches to this problem, flat-minima optimization treats the Gaussians as trainable parameters and steers training toward flat minima, which generalize better, by perturbing the Gaussians with random noise or along the training gradient. However, these perturbations ignore their direction relative to the other training views. Interestingly, we find that the direction of the perturbation determines whether it improves generalization. Specifically, we decompose the gradient of each training view into a component parallel to the average gradient of all views, on which the views agree, and an orthogonal component, on which they disagree. Perturbing along the orthogonal component improves generalization, whereas perturbing along the parallel component does not. We further find that the flatness correction often opposes the reconstruction gradient, shrinking or even reversing the reconstruction step. Based on these findings, we propose DecoFlat, which perturbs each Gaussian along the orthogonal component together with random noise. Furthermore, we introduce a conflict-aware correction, which removes the part of the flatness correction that opposes the reconstruction gradient, and a rescheduling of the spherical-harmonics color, which suppresses the overfitting of view-dependent appearance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DecoFlat, as a plug-in optimizer, consistently improves vanilla 3DGS and a wide range of sparse-view 3DGS methods.

papers.title: ArgsWorld: Unifying 3DGS Scene Reconstruction, Generation and Extrapolation with Autoregressive Diffusion Transformer
papers.authors: Weiming Chen; Shuaiyan Liu; Xinyu Shao; Zhewen Chen; Tian Guan et al.
papers.abstract: Autoregressive diffusion world models deliver strong video generation performance, yet they typically output only RGB frames rather than explicit 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) scene representations, creating a gap between learned visual world dynamics and usable 3D assets for downstream robotics, simulation and rendering. To bridge this gap, we introduce ArgsWorld, an autoregressive diffusion model that also produces an explicit 3DGS scene. For each generation chunk, the diffusion transformer jointly processes clean historical image latents and noisy latents for new views. It keeps the historical image latents fixed and refreshes the scene features so that the Gaussian representation can be revised as new regions come into view. Our 3D Self-Forcing Distillation trains the model on its own generated histories using a mixture of single-view and multi-view data. Distribution matching supervises direct image latents and latents of Gaussian renderings at both generation and additional cameras. ArgsWorld unifies 3D scene reconstruction from posed images, scene generation from image or text prompts, and scene extrapolation across camera segments with disconnected endpoints. Experimental results demonstrate that ArgsWorld achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple 3D scene modeling tasks. Project page: https://m4a1tastegood.github.io/ArgsWorld/

papers.title: VeilGS: Solving Darkness as a Veil of 2D Basis Maps over Retinex 3DGS
papers.authors: Mohab Kishawy; Chengzhou Tang; Shahram Shirani; Jun Chen
papers.abstract: In a dark capture, the darkness is not uniform. How much light reaches a surface depends on where it lies relative to the few light sources, and the camera compresses what remains with a tone curve. Most low-light 3D reconstruction methods either apply one curve to every pixel of a view, so a dark object beside a lamp and a bright one in an unlit corner receive the same correction, or store the darkness in the 3D representation, where it can absorb scene detail. We present VeilGS, a 3D Gaussian Splatting method for low-light novel view synthesis that treats the degradation as a veil drawn over a clear scene. Each Gaussian carries an albedo and a shading latent instead of spherical harmonics, separating surface colour from illumination. Each view is darkened by a spatially varying gain followed by a global tone curve, and rendering without this veil gives the restored scene. A small network predicts a coarse basis for the gain from the observation, and its coefficients are solved for each view rather than learned. Training through this solve discourages the Gaussians from absorbing what the veil can explain. VeilGS needs no paired normal-light supervision and stores no per-view parameters. On Gaussian-DK, its restored renders score best on no-reference NIQE and CLIP-IQA and are rated highest in a blind user study with 55 participants. On LOM, it achieves results competitive with the state of the art.

papers.title: PennyGS: Full Resolution 3DGS Training in Minutes on Consumer GPUs
papers.authors: Nicholas Jing Shou Nge; Yuang Shi; Geraldine Morin; Simone Gasparini; Anand Bhojan et al.
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting is increasingly fed by high-resolution captures from commodity devices, yet training still happens at reduced resolution with research-grade GPUs. We present PennyGS, a method to achieve full-resolution (4K) training of 3DGS on consumer GPUs by improving the efficiency of every stage of a training step. Improvements include a leaner splat with flat RGB color and a directional cone opacity, fused projection and key emission, forward rasterization optimizations with strided pixel sampling, an approximate tile SSIM loss, a warp-per-splat backward rasterization, and a fused backward projection and sparse Adam step. At the standard 30k-step budget, PennyGS is the fastest of 10 methods on Mip-NeRF 360 and Tanks&Temples 4K on all four GPUs at competitive quality, at least 3.9x faster than the quickest of the others, while peaking below 2 GB of GPU memory. On an RTX 3060, a full-resolution Mip-NeRF 360 scene trains in 6m 25s, faster than any other method trains it on an RTX 4090.

papers.title: Multi-View Transformer with Geometry-Guided Multi-Modal ControlNet for 3D Virtual Try-On
papers.authors: Sarthak Batra; Armin Mustafa; Adrian Hilton
papers.abstract: Editing a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) capture of a person so that they wear a new garment requires every rendered view to agree on the same garment details. Existing 3D virtual try-on (VTON) pipelines, however, edit training views largely independently and fuse them with hand-designed heuristics such as manually chosen reference views and fixed attention-blending weights. The resulting inconsistencies are baked into the 3D representation and surface as texture drift, blurred prints, and implausible geometry in novel views. We present GS-VTON-MVT, a three-stage framework that combines implicit and explicit 3D reasoning for consistent 3DGS try-on. (i) A multi-view inpainting transformer jointly edits a set of training views with full cross-view self-attention, so that cross-view correspondence is learned rather than imposed. (ii) A geometry-guided multi-modal ControlNet conditions the diffusion editor on the garment image together with depth and surface normals rendered from the current 3DGS state, supplying explicit structure where visual evidence is weakest. (iii) A pose-adaptive persona-aware attention replaces the fixed blending weight between current-view and reference-view features with weights derived from camera-pose proximity. On the 3D-VTONBench benchmark, GS-VTON-MVT improves FID, KID, LPIPS-based cross-view consistency, and user preference over general-purpose 3D editors and prior 3D try-on methods.

papers.title: AGSR: Aperture-Guided Super-Resolution for Gaussian Splatting
papers.authors: Ayman Alkhateeb; Hadi Amirpour; Christian Timmerer
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables real-time novel view synthesis, but Gaussian rasterization attenuates fine-scale scene structure through the projected covariance of each primitive. We show that contracting these projected covariances at inference time can mitigate the effective bandwidth limitation induced by finite Gaussian footprints, motivating a multi-aperture rendering framework for super-resolution.   Based on this insight, we propose AGSR (Aperture-Guided Super-Resolution), a lightweight inference-time framework that progressively fuses multi-aperture renderings using uncertainty-guided feature aggregation and geometric conditioning from transmittance and depth cues. AGSR operates as a plug-in enhancement for pre-trained 3DGS models.   Experiments on the Mip-NeRF 360 benchmark show that AGSR outperforms lightweight image-space super-resolution baselines, with gains increasing as the underlying Gaussian representation deteriorates. The results provide evidence that covariance contraction exposes bandwidth-sensitive structural cues attenuated by native Gaussian rasterization. AGSR achieves these improvements while maintaining real-time performance with up to 139k parameters.

papers.title: Multi-View Relighting with Mergeable Radiance Fields
papers.authors: Yinan Wang; Rohan Kadkol; Hyunjin Yoo; Jean-François Lalonde; James J. Clark
papers.abstract: We propose MergeableRF, a method for radiance field relighting through model parameter merging. Given multi-view images of a scene under known basis lights, our goal is to relight the scene by directly combining the parameters of radiance fields trained under these lights. This is motivated by the linearity of light transport: the image under a mixture of lights is the same weighted combination of the images under each light. However, combining the parameters of independently trained radiance fields does not produce the corresponding combination of images. To address this, we represent a scene with shared geometry and a separate appearance network for each basis light. We start these networks from the same initialization and introduce merge-aware training, which teaches their parameter combinations to reproduce the corresponding combinations of images. Given a target HDR environment map, we compute its basis-light coefficients and use them to merge the appearance networks into a single relit model. Our method supports both Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), without material estimation, additional relighting networks, or target-specific optimization. Unlike image-space blending, it requires only one rendering pass per viewpoint. Experiments on synthetic Neural Gaffer objects and real OLATverse captures demonstrate relighting quality competitive with methods trained on the same multi-light observations.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Onboard Vision-Language-Navigation Framework for Aerial Robots in Complex Environments
papers.authors: Yuze Wu; Mo Zhu; Xingxing Li; Yuheng Du; Zhaoqi Wang et al.
papers.abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are expected to achieve semantic reasoning, intelligent decision-making, and long-horizon navigation under strict onboard constraints. While recent foundation-model-driven approaches have shown promising progress toward this goal, existing methods remain limited by challenges in 3D data availability, trajectory feasibility, long-horizon reasoning, and computational efficiency in complex environments. To bridge these gaps, we propose VLN-AR, a hierarchical vision-language-navigation (VLN) framework for aerial robots. VLN-AR decouples multimodal reasoning and low-level control, enabling structured prediction of 3D pose commands and navigation intentions that are translated into dynamically feasible actions. To mitigate data scarcity and domain gaps, we introduce a fully automated 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)-based pipeline to generate scalable photorealistic UAV navigation data. A progressive three-stage training strategy further enhances grounding, scene reasoning, and complex navigation. In addition, a lightweight cognitive agent improves long-horizon reasoning via memory-aware task decomposition. Finally, we design onboard optimization techniques, including token sparsification and model lightweighting, achieving 7.1x-9.4x speedup while maintaining high navigation performance on resource-limited UAV platforms. Experiments show great improvements over existing methods in both simulation and real-world UAV navigation. Project website: https://wyz000.github.io/VLN-AR/

papers.title: GC-GS: Optimizing 3D Gaussian Splatting with Gradient Conflict as a Geometry Signal
papers.authors: Chenhao Zhang; Fengze Zhang; Fengqing Zhu
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is commonly optimized with multiple reconstruction losses, which naturally forms a multi-objective optimization problem. This issue becomes more pronounced when perceptual losses are introduced to improve visual quality, as different objectives may impose competing update directions on Gaussian primitives and make it difficult to simultaneously improve fidelity, perceptual quality, and representation efficiency. Based on this view, we reformulate 3DGS training as a multi-objective optimization problem and derive selective conflict-aware position updates that reduce interference between competing objectives while preserving the contribution of each loss.
